name: arcade-buylist-probe
note: PROBE, not the measurement. Finds a --buy list that actually BUILDS and USES an arcade under the headless autopilot, so the real --noplay A/B (matrix-arcade16) is not pointed at towns with no machines - a null result that reads like 'the arcade costs nothing'. All arms are AS-BUILT (occupancy on): the number that matters is `arcade.playedIn` (towns where >=1 game was played = built AND staffed AND a bored, funded customer reached it). Staffing needs >=2 shack crabs on a shift, so a used arcade needs the arcade built PLUS ~2 chef hires - which is why order matters. Four buy lists x {30d, 40d}, one 16-town block each (16 is plenty to read a build/play FRACTION; the escape delta is the measurement's job, not the probe's). batch.mjs's new arcade instrument reports built/playedIn/games. 30-day arms answer the bead's window directly; 40-day arms diagnose whether a weak result is a TIME problem or a fundamental one.
